spec_family.name: New Construction Stair Riser & Stringer Painting
spec_family.description: Combined prime+paint spec for stair risers and stringers/skirtboards in new construction. Covers 4 substrates (MDF, poplar, hardwood, paint-grade plywood) with substrate-driven primer selection and QT-driven finish systems. Primer is conditional on substrate_state: SS_BARE requires primer, SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips to finish coats. Dual UOM system: risers use EA, stringers use LF. Stringer_type (open/closed) is a configuration dimension affecting production rates. Stairwell access modifiers from PaintScope Stairwell Geometry System apply to stringer work. Canonical painting sequence enforced: stringers (#4) before risers (#8). Tread protection mandatory from Day 1. Material systems are QT-driven recommendations — contractor retains discretion on product selection.

includes: Riser face priming and painting (vertical surface between treads)
Stringer/skirtboard priming and painting (diagonal transition element between stairs and wall)
Surface prep per substrate (sanding, dust removal, grain fill on MDF cut edges)
Stringer-to-wall caulking (mandatory joint for closed stringers)
Riser-to-stringer caulking (2 joints per riser at left/right stringer edges)
MDF edge sealing with solvent-based sealer (bare MDF only — step 1 of two-step prime)
Primer coat — conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE
Finish coat application (brush or spray) — 2 coats standard, 3+ at QT5 brush/roll per FFD 15.10.3
Between-coat interstage process (inspect, sand, repair, clean) at ALL quality tiers
Tread protection setup and maintenance (mandatory from Day 1 through cleanup)
Wall masking along stringer edge (spray method)
Protection teardown (tread covers may be deferred if railing/tread work follows)

excludes.item: Stair treads (floor-rated coating, absolutely last per doctrine)

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, repair scope, and coat count. Does NOT affect application quality (binary at all tiers). Does NOT drive primer selection (substrate-driven).
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2 not applicable — stairways are scrutinized, prominent surfaces per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 10.1. QT3=standard production. QT4=premium (full sand, systematic inspect). QT5=superior (thorough sand, critical inspect, 3+ coats brush/roll). Sheen/QT gate enforced at runtime.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for primer and finish coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default for stair component detail work. Spray available for large-scope NC production but requires wall masking along stringer edge.

configuration_dimensions.description: Finish sheen. Constrained by quality tier gate.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Default semi-gloss requires minimum QT4. Semi-gloss default for risers (toe-kick scuff resistance per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 7.2). If user selects QT3, semi-gloss is rejected and satin offered. Gloss is QT5 only.

configuration_dimensions.description: Riser/stringer substrate material. Drives prep protocol and primer selection.
configuration_dimensions.notes: MDF is most common NC riser/stringer material. MDF edges need solvent-based sealer. Poplar requires stain-blocking (mandatory). Hardwood requires tannin-blocking. Plywood gets standard primer-sealer.

configuration_dimensions.description: Input substrate condition. Drives primer requirement and prep scope.
configuration_dimensions.notes: SS_BARE: full primer coat required, heavier prep (full sand). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: skip primer, lighter prep (scuff sand only). Standard NC trim arrives pre-primed from mill.

configuration_dimensions.description: Stringer profile type. Controls production rate modifier for stringer tasks.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Open stringers have notched profile visible from exposed side — more surface area, complex geometry. 1.4x is midpoint of 1.3-1.5x range. Closed stringers are flat boards against wall (like baseboard). Open stringer modifier applies to ALL stringer tasks (prep, prime, finish, sanding).

paintable_items.name: Stair riser face
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count each individual riser as one EA. Riser count sourced from PaintScope Stairwell Geometry System riser count (PS_META.STAIRWELL.RISERS). Riser SF per unit = stairwell_width × riser_height (typically 3.5 ft × 0.625 ft ≈ 2.2 SF). EA used for labor; SF derived for material quantity.
paintable_items.notes: Risers are uniform within a flight — no Size Bucket Method needed. Simple EA counting. Risers are always H1 (accessible from adjacent treads).

paintable_items.name: Stringer / skirtboard
paintable_items.counting_rules: Measure total LF of stringer/skirtboard runs. Derivable from PaintScope Stairwell Geometry System rake_length (PS_STAIRWELL.RAKE_LENGTH_FT) × number of stringer runs. Enclosed stair = 2 runs; open one side = 1 wall-side run (exposed side may differ). 1 LF ≈ 1 SF per PDCA standard for linear trim.
paintable_items.notes: Stringer_type (open/closed) affects production rate but not counting. Stairwell access modifiers apply based on max_working_height.

variants.notes: Bare substrate, standard brush production. Primer + 2 finish coats. Satin is the only sheen at QT3.
Bare substrate, premium brush. Primer + 2 finish coats. Semi-gloss typical at QT4.
Bare substrate, superior brush with gloss. Primer + 3 finish coats per FFD 15.10.3. 4 total coats, 3 interstage cycles.
Factory-primed, standard brush. No primer — scuff sand then 2 finish coats. Most common NC scenario.
Factory-primed, premium brush. No primer — 2 finish coats.
Factory-primed, superior brush with gloss. 3 finish coats per FFD 15.10.3.
Factory-primed, standard spray. Full protection required. Fastest production.
Factory-primed, superior spray. QT5 spray uses 2 coats (not 3). Full protection.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of individual stair risers to paint. Sourced from PaintScope Stairwell Geometry System riser count (PS_META.STAIRWELL.RISERS). Standard flight = 12-16 risers.
Total LF of stringer/skirtboard runs. Derivable from geometry system rake_length × number of stringer runs.
Stringer-to-wall caulk junction LF. Closed stringers only — same LF as stringer where it meets wall.
Tread protection area — mandatory. Sourced from PaintScope Asset Catalog Section 8. Tread count = risers - 1.
Landing floor protection area. Drop cloth runners at landing areas.
Wall masking LF along stringer top edge for spray method.

protection_zones_required.condition: ALWAYS — mandatory regardless of application method
protection_zones_required.notes: Mandatory from Day 1. Ram Board Stair Armor or equivalent non-slip protection. NEVER use plastic sheeting on treads — extreme fall hazard per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2. Tread protection removal may be deferred if railing/tread work follows.
Canvas drop cloth runners at landing areas. Excluded when landing floor is subfloor.
Wall masking along stringer top edge for spray method. Also required for brush when walls are SS_PAINTED_* (finished).

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Treads are above and below each riser. Treads may be stain-grade or floor-rated coating — different system from trim enamel on risers. Treads painted last per doctrine. Protection only — no edge painting task.

Stringer meets wall at full length. Stringer-to-wall caulk joint mandatory for closed stringers. Color drenching (stringer matches wall) possible per doctrine Section 7.3 but finish product is still enamel, not wall paint.
Stringer connects to baseboard at top and bottom of flight. Same finish group — same color/sheen typically. Landing baseboard routed to SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT.

valid_input_states.notes: Combined prime+paint spec. SS_BARE (bare wood/plywood) requires full primer coat + heavier prep (full sand, substrate-specific primer). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY (standard NC mill-primed trim) requires scuff sand only — skip primer, go directly to finish coats.

output_state.notes: Output state varies by sheen dimension. Semi-gloss is default (requires QT4+).

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Unfinished walls need no protection during brush application. Typical NC scenario.
Spray method requires wall masking even on unfinished walls to prevent overspray.
When walls are finished (SS_PAINTED_*), wall masking along stringer required for BOTH methods.
Treads ALWAYS protected regardless of state. Mandatory from Day 1. Painted absolutely last or may be stain-grade.

site_condition_rules.effect: Floor protection excluded when landing floor is subfloor.
site_condition_rules.notes: NC may have subfloor during stair painting. Finished/partial floors require canvas drop cloth runners at landings.

site_condition_rules.effect: Additional protection when occupied. Tread protection already mandatory; may need additional signage and barriers.
site_condition_rules.notes: Rare in NC. When occupied, stairway access management critical for safety.

site_condition_rules.effect: Lead-safe practices for sanding tasks. tested_positive=2.0x, unknown_pre1978=1.5x.
site_condition_rules.notes: Rare in NC (post-1978). RRP protocol triggered if applicable.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Stair riser/stringer painting is part of the trim package in NC. Typical project sequence: Prime ceilings → Prime walls → Finish ceilings → Trim/stair/window package (prime → finish) → Wall finish. Pairs naturally with SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT for shared finish group and SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC for shared staging.
sequencing_notes.canonical_internal_sequence: Within every module: stringers (#4) completed before risers (#8) per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 3.2. Painting stringers first avoids contact with wet riser surfaces when moving between treads.
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Tread protection FIRST (before any other work) → Landing floor protection → Wall masking (spray) → Apply coats → Teardown wall mask → Teardown floor drops → Teardown tread covers LAST. Tread cover removal may be deferred if railing/tread work follows.
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Prep (substrate-specific) → [MDF edge seal if applicable] → [Primer (conditional on SS_BARE)] → [Interstage] → Finish coat 1 → Interstage → Finish coat 2 → [QT5 brush: Interstage → Finish coat 3] → Final inspect → Cleanup

relationships.notes: Stair riser/stringer painting is part of the trim package in NC. Same crew, same material system, same session as other trim. Treads are ALWAYS the final stair component per doctrine Section 3.2. Railing work shares staging and tread protection.

sections_used: Section 6.2 — Tread Protection (Ram Board Stair Armor)
Section 7.2 — Sheen Architecture (semi-gloss default for risers)

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Dry times should be specified in specs
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: No dry times in specs — refer to product PDS. Dry times vary by product, temperature, humidity.

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Material system selection is mandatory doctrine — QT drives material system
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: Material systems are suggestions per QT — contractor has discretion on product selection.

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Waterborne alkyds have longer open time
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: Both Advance (waterborne alkyd) and Emerald Urethane (acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd) have SHORT working times. Fast dry demands proper first-pass technique.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for NC stair riser & stringer painting (Spec #11 in Phase 1 catalog). Key features: combined prime+paint with conditional primer (substrate-driven primer, QT-driven finish), 4 substrates (MDF, poplar, hardwood, paint-grade plywood), dual UOM system (EA for risers, LF for stringers), stringer_type (open/closed) configuration dimension with 1.4x open modifier, canonical painting sequence (stringers #4 before risers #8), mandatory tread protection (Ram Board Stair Armor), 5 substrate-driven primer paths (including MDF two-step prime), 3 QT-driven finish systems (reused from trim/window specs), stairwell access modifiers for stringers (1.3x-2.8x), 30 SOP tasks across 7 modules, 3 round configurations, 3 protection zones, 9 variants. First spec with dual UOM (EA + LF) for different paintable items.
